summary.headline: Orchid Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR341 crore, gross margin recovered to about 39% and EBITDA rose 148% to INR52 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 14% YoY to INR341 crore, with sequential growth of about 12%. Gross margin rose about 8 percentage points to roughly 39%, helped by normalisation after last year's high-cost inventory write-offs. EBITDA including other income rose to INR52 crore (15% margin) despite higher fuel and energy costs and two one-off items of about INR5 crore each (an expected credit loss provision and a merger-related impairment). Management said the recovery is not expected to be a straight line, with pricing and demand in core markets still competitive.

segments.name: Cephalosporin API / core business
segments.commentary: Management said injectables showed recovery in the latest quarter while oral cephalosporins still face weak demand and excess capacity. Orchid's complex injectables with no competition in India are supporting gross margin.

segments.name: AMS (antimicrobial stewardship) platform
segments.commentary: Quarterly EBITDA drag reduced to about INR1.5 crore. Portfolio is 15 distinct products and 18 SKUs; more than 120 hospitals on regular business, with about 10-15% quarterly growth.

segments.name: EXBLIFEP (licensing and royalties)
segments.commentary: Current run rate of royalties and milestones is about $3-4 million per year. Russia estimated 10-year sales about $178 million and Latin America (first licence, 8-9 countries) about $80 million. UK launch pending.

segments.name: Cefiderocol project
segments.commentary: INR173 crore invested as of 30 Sep 2026. Commissioning targeted Dec 2026, inauguration on 18 Jan 2027, India launch targeted Q3 FY27 subject to validation and approvals. Manufacturing fee basis around 20-25% PBT.

segments.name: 7-ACA project (Jammu)
segments.commentary: Plant designed for 1,000 metric tons per annum; commercial operations scheduled for March 2027. Cost overrun attributed to commodity price increases over the last six to eight months.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give profit margin guidance as a matter of policy; aims to keep gross margin above 35%, managed through product mix.
Merger integration savings expected to start becoming visible towards end of FY27.
Three to four additional EXBLIFEP licence agreements hoped for over the next two quarters; these are in discussion only.
Middle East and South Africa launches now expected by Q1 CY2027.
Second half expected to be better than first half, consistent with past trend, though management said the market has been erratic.
Five or six products targeted by 2030 in the US filing pipeline; ANDA filings at least six to eight months away.
capex_capacity: Cefiderocol: manufacturing to be completed by March 2027; DCGI licence application afterwards, with at least six months expected; commercialisation hoped for September-October 2027.

7-ACA Jammu: 1,000 MTPA plant, commercial operations scheduled March 2027; pilot technology validated and yield improvement work continuing. Management said ramp-up to full utilisation in two quarters is unlikely.
Capacity utilisation: Dhanuka facility about 80-90%, Orchid about 60% (after debottlenecking). Plans to rationalise duplicated capacity and allow either plant to supply any product.
Board approved a potential fundraise; proceeds to fund 7-ACA cost overrun, repay cefiderocol project debt, and downstream product investment in Chennai (environmental clearance now obtained).
demand_pricing: 7-ACA prices have stayed around $50 +/-10% over five to six years; management says the current rupee depreciation favours the company.
Europe demand described as weak; company gained some customers after a competitor's import alert, but the gain was small.
Cefixime pricing and competition remain largely unchanged, with marginal improvement only.
Oral cephalosporins face excess capacity and the market has consolidated to three players; management expects pricing to rationalise over time.
Enmetazobactam approved in Middle East in February 2026; launches delayed by war, ramp-up not yet happening.

qa_highlights.question: Is adjusted EBITDA about INR34 crore for Q2 after excluding the two INR5 crore one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that this understanding is correct.

qa_highlights.question: What was the other income jump in Q2, and what was the royalty income?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income rose due to non-cephalosporin Dhanuka products and formulations, plus the sale of old Orchid intangible assets. Current royalty and milestone run rate is about $3-4 million per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US EXBLIFEP deal close?
qa_highlights.answer: No; US talks are preliminary with no timeline. Three to four further deals refer to advanced discussions in other markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the fundraise and use of proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed timeline or mode yet. Proceeds to cover the 7-ACA cost overrun, repay cefiderocol project debt, and fund downstream products in Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cefiderocol India licence position and margin model?
qa_highlights.answer: The licence covers 135 low and middle income countries including India; GARDP and Shionogi are near signing an India marketing licence. Manufacturing is on a fixed 20-25% PBT basis, with a separate marketing margin under negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Can 7-ACA reach full utilisation within two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called that wishful thinking given earlier entrants' fermentation problems, but said it is taking remedial action.

risks_watch: Gross margin sustainability: depends on product mix; oral cephalosporin pricing remains under pressure.
Fuel and power costs up about 30% YoY because of Middle East conflict; the EXBLIFEP launch timeline in the Middle East and South Africa depends on the region.
7-ACA ramp-up and yield targets, plus the cost overrun. The March 2027 commercial start is at risk.
Cefiderocol India launch depends on validation, manufacturing licence, DCGI approval and clinical trial waiver.
Planned fundraise size, timing and mode not disclosed; the US EXBLIFEP deal has no timeline.
Management gives no profit margin or next-year guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the EXBLIFEP licensing and royalty build-out and on the cefiderocol timeline, but cautious on near-term pricing and on 7-ACA ramp-up. Evasive on fundraise size, timing and the US deal, and it declined to give margin or next-year quantitative guidance.
key_quotes: Even after absorbing these items, profit after tax was INR28.6 crores in Q2 of '27 against a loss of INR0.9 crores in Q2 of '26, with earnings per share of INR4.77.
Pricing and demand in our core markets remain competitive.
So, we don't give any profit margin guidance as an organization policy.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin about 39% in Q2 (up 8 pp YoY) and H2 expected better than H1, with merger savings visible toward end-FY27, but power and fuel costs are up about 30% and management says recovery will not be a straight line; EBITDA excl. one-offs about INR34 crore on INR341 crore revenue (about 10%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cefiderocol manufacturing (INR173 crore invested, commissioning targeted Dec 2026, inauguration 18 Jan 2027) and 7-ACA Jammu 1,000 MTPA plant (commercial operations scheduled March 2027) are both under construction, though 7-ACA ramp to full utilisation in two quarters is unlikely.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 14% YoY to INR341 crore and H1 was up 15%, with AMS growing 10-15% a quarter across 120+ hospitals and 7-ACA and cefiderocol volumes added, but Orchid base plant is only at about 60% utilisation and Europe demand is weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved a potential fundraise to fund the 7-ACA overrun, cefiderocol debt repayment and Chennai downstream products, but size, timing and mode are undisclosed; base plant utilisation is only about 60% so a new greenfield capex is unlikely even though Dhanuka runs at 80-90%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Only a gross margin floor of above 35% was given (H1 FY27 gross margin about 36%) with no revenue guidance; management called the market erratic and pricing still competitive.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management gives no margin or next-year guidance, oral cephalosporin pricing is still weak with excess capacity, fuel and power costs are up about 30% YoY, and 7-ACA March 2027 start is at risk from cost overrun and yield issues.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cefiderocol India launch targeted Q3 FY27 subject to validation and approvals, though DCGI approval (at least six months after manufacturing) and the September-October 2027 commercialisation point to slippage risk; EXBLIFEP Middle East and South Africa launches now expected by Q1 CY2027.

rows.label: EXBLIFEP additional licence deals
rows.why: Management hopes for three to four more licence agreements over two quarters, but these are only in discussion, and US talks are preliminary with no timeline; current royalty run rate is about $3-4 million per year.

rows.label: Cefixime and injectables recovery
rows.why: Injectables showed recovery in the latest quarter and complex injectables with no Indian competition support gross margin, while cefixime pricing has only marginally improved and oral cephalosporins have excess capacity.

rows.label: Working capital release
rows.why: Working capital days fell to 118 from 137 and receivable days to 100 from 113, with working capital down to INR412 crore from INR464 crore and H1 operating cash flow of about INR118 crore.
